newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Explosion sets Bangladesh gas field ablaze.
newsitem.headline: Explosion sets Bangladesh gas field ablaze.

text.p: An explosion set ablaze a gas field in northeast Bangladesh on Sunday, forcing hundreds of people to flee the flames and injuring at least four, officials and witnesses said.

Flames leapt 300-500 feet (100-150 metres) into the air, according to an official statement on the accident, and specialist fire-fighters and experts were called in from Singapore and the United States.
The casualties were Bangladeshis working on the rig at Mugrachhara in Moulvi Bazar district, where U.S. company Occidental Petroleum Corp began drilling early this month, officials said.
Energy Ministry officials said the accident occurred when the pipeline of the rig hit a "trap gas" layer at a depth of 840 metres (2,755 feet).
Experts with fire fighting equipment from Singapore would arrive on Monday to try to extinguish the blaze, Energy Secretary Tawfiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury told Reuters.
He said another expert team from Occidental headquaters in Houston, Texas, would arrive shortly to assess the extent of damage and find out when drilling could be resumed.
Witnesses said fire broke out at the drilling site following an explosion in a well at about 1.45 a.m. on Sunday, they said.
Mosharraf Hossain, chairman of state-run oil and gas agency Petrobangla, told Reuters on Sunday night there was no explosion but the fire was caused by leakage.
"We are uncertain when drilling would resume but expect the blaze would die down soon," he said.
Chowdhury and Hossain both said all equipment at the rig had been destroyed.
The fire was within 150 feet (50 metres) of the drilling well, the statement said.
Local journalists said several workers at the gas field were injured, and vehicles and staff barracks gutted.
Occidental, which has won the right for exploration of hydrocarbon in the Sylhet region, began drilling on June 2.
Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan has postponed a scheduled official visit to Iran because of the accident. Khan and senior officials will visit the accident site on Monday.
Officials in Moulavi Bazar, some 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Sylhet, said they saw fire above the forest at Magurchhara gas field at around 2 a.m.
Railway tracks passing by the gas field also caught fire, disrupting train services.

Journalists said the fire spread over a 2 km (mile) area around the gas field, 20 km (12 miles) from Moulvi Bazar. Police surrounded the whole area and prohibited visits except by experts and officials.
They said some 200 people worked in the Magurchhara gas field. Witnesses told reporters they saw people, many apparently hurt, fleeing the fire.
Workers at two nearby tea gardens and villagers fled in panic, they said.
"The blaze could spread further as surrounding areas are covered with dense forest," one journalist said.
Occidental officials in Dhaka were not immediately available for details.

Occidental was offered the right to search for hydrocarbons in the entire Sylhet region, bordering India's Meghalaya and Assam states, under a Production Sharing Contract (PSC) with the Bangladesh government.
Occidental said it would spend up to $100 million in exploring three out of 23 blocs that Bangladesh has earmarked for foreign hydrocarbon firms.
The government has ordered an inquiry into the fire, and asked mmigration and customs authorities to extend help to incoming Occidental expert teams.
